node.title: Re: Parse for a name after a keyword search in all the files, given directory as input
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [prash_sri],

In your code, you are using [doc://open] instead of [doc://opendir], this won't work. If you had [doc://warnings] turned on, you would have been warned about this, see [id://111088]. Also, as documented in [doc://readdir], you should prepend the name of the directory to the filename, and note that it will return every entry in the directory, including subdirectories, which you can filter with perl's [doc://-X|-f] filetest operator, and including the special directories . and .., which you can filter with [doc://File::Spec]'s no_upwards (although the aforementioned -f test would filter them too). See the examples under [doc://readdir].

Trying to write a perl code which browses all the files recursively under a given input directory

If by recursively you mean that you want to look into subdirectories too, then I would recommend [doc://File::Find] over [doc://readdir]/[doc://opendir], or perhaps one of the easier-to-use modules [mod://File::Find::Rule], [mod://Path::Class]'s recurse function, or [mod://Path::Tiny]'s visit function. Personally I like [mod://Path::Class], but I can recommend any of the modules I mentioned here.

Regards,
-- Hauke D

Update: s/including \Kdir/subdir/
